purpose: Confirm that search version and sequence metadata flags add per-hit concurrency fields which the gateway must not silently omit or approximate
environment: Separate single-node containers with security disabled
reproduction: Start each recorded image as an isolated single-node container with its security plugin disabled.
Create hit-metadata-probe with title mapped as text and category mapped as keyword.
Index document 1 with refresh=true, then update its category once with refresh=true.
POST hit-metadata-probe/_search with request_with_metadata and inspect each hit's _version, _seq_no, and _primary_term.
Repeat with request_without_metadata and verify those three fields are absent.
Send version as the JSON string true and record the observed coercion separately from the gateway's stricter validation policy.
limitations: This is request and response compatibility evidence, not a concurrent-write or conditional-update test.
The numeric values come from one primary shard and one update; they establish field presence and change tracking but are not portable constants.
The probe does not claim that Elasticsearch and OpenSearch token histories remain identical under replication, failover, bulk writes, or other engine versions.
No Qdrant endpoint was involved in the native observations. Gateway rejection is validated separately with a mocked upstream that records calls.
